I am writing this review to express my profound disappointment with the service I received at this GP practice. After moving into the area, and living directly across the road from the surgery, I was encouraged by my support team to register both myself and my newborn daughter. As a mother rebuilding my life after escaping abuse, currently in temporary refuge accommodation and transitioning into my permanent home, it was essential for us to have a GP within walking distance.

My newborn daughter has Down Syndrome, and I have no family or friends nearby for support. My situation requires stability, accessibility, and a practice that shows basic human compassion. Unfortunately, my experience here was the opposite.

When I arrived and calmly tried to explain my circumstances to the receptionist — including the fact that I had been temporarily placed in a women’s refuge and was now settling into a permanent home — I was met with rudeness, dismissiveness, and a complete lack of empathy. The staff did not listen, did not attempt to understand, and made no effort to help.

Instead, I was abruptly told that I “can get the bus” back to the GP I was previously registered with, despite the fact that I now live across the road from this practice and have a newborn with additional needs. For a mother who is trying to rebuild her life, stay safe, and provide stability for her children, this response was not only unhelpful — it was shocking.

I have overcome significant challenges, including addiction recovery, rebuilding my confidence, and caring for my baby entirely on my own. The very least I expected was a baseline level of respect and consideration. Instead, I left feeling dismissed, judged, and completely unsupported.
